media.title: Late night deploy went green. Three weeks of work. This is the moment that makes all the context-switching worth it. ✅
Morning walk before deep work. Non-negotiable. The best ideas never come at the keyboard. 🌿
Reading corner. 'Thinking in Systems' by Donella Meadows. Changing how I see every production incident I've ever worked on. 📚
Team offsite in Coorg. Six months async-first, first time meeting half the team in person. The relationship is the foundation. Everything else is process. 🌄
Keyboard arrived. Yes, it matters. When you type 8 hours a day, the tool is not a luxury. ⌨️
First PR merged to a major OSS project after three rejected attempts. Persistence and listening. Open source is the best CS education available. 🚀
Sunday cooking. Parallel processing applies in the kitchen too. Two dishes, one time window, same result as sequential but faster. Engineering brain doesn't switch off. 🍳
Desk setup after the upgrade. Monitor arm changed my posture, my focus, and my output. Invest in the environment. 🖥️
Six months of Rust. The borrow checker went from prison to safety net. Paradigm shifts require discomfort first. ⚡
Conference talk done. Standing room. Questions from people building real things. This is the energy I show up for. 🎤
Hiking in Coorg clears the cache. Technical problems that were stuck for days look completely different after three hours in the hills. 🏔️
Mentorship call 50 this year. I learn as much from these conversations as the mentee does. Teaching is learning in disguise. 🤝
Filter coffee + distributed systems paper. Saturday morning ritual. 10/10 recommend. ☕
Shipped the async communication guide to the team. First week: uncomfortable. Second week: productive. Now we can't imagine going back. 📝
Bangalore traffic on the way to a client meeting. Two hours I'll never recover. This is why async-first exists. 🚗
EOY retrospective with the team. We listed what went well before what to improve. Deliberately. Humans are wired for negativity. Counter it intentionally. 🎯
Late night reading. Sleep is not optional. This is a reminder to myself. 📖
